authorityAudit.detail: D-136 owes a later MF-6 updating DR-133's stale no-contract clause while keeping the row OPEN. It supports the cell content but does not authorize combining H1 with H2.
D-138 owes the DR-131 MF-6 as a later act and explicitly says it is its own D-000 cycle and commit. D-140 combines that act with DR-133's MF-6 without declaring a supersession.
The H section says: 'These may run in any order. Each is its own later D-000 cycle and commit.' It then identifies H1 as DR-133's MF-6 and H2 as DR-131's MF-6. D-140 performs H1 and H2 in one act.

The live entry incorporates the frozen turn-2 subject by digest and summarizes H as the D-136/D-138 MF-6 cells. D-140 relies on the subject's H1/H2 names for authority, so it cannot ignore the same subject's per-item cycle-and-commit restriction.

They require review of file-08 edits but do not silently supersede D-139's more specific preference-laden sequencing choice. A scoped successor could change that choice, but D-140 declares itself rule-governed and does not identify any superseded clause.

mustFix.impact: Adopting D-140 as written would silently override a specific, adopted, preference-laden sequencing constraint while describing the decision as merely rule-governed execution. It would also violate D-138's row-specific own-cycle requirement. The otherwise-correct cell edits therefore lack authority in their proposed combined form.
requiredRepair: Preferred: scope this cycle to exactly one of H1 or H2, and run the other MF-6 in its own later D-000 cycle and commit, as D-139 requires.

Alternative: explicitly make the proposal a scoped preference-laden successor to D-139's per-H cycle-and-commit rule (and to D-138's own-cycle clause for H2), state the exact superseded text, justify batching, and review that successor under D-000 before applying either cell edit.

reversibilityAudit.detail: Restoring the two no-contract clauses would mechanically reverse the proposed edits, but reversibility does not cure the missing authority to combine acts that were required to receive separate cycles and commits.

consentRule: CONSENT only if there are no MUST-FIX or SHOULD-FIX findings.
coordinatorSummary: OBJECT. The proposed Status-cell text, live before-cells, digests, zero-readiness effect, and non-SATISFIED boundaries all check out. One authority defect blocks adoption: D-140 batches D-139 H1 and H2 even though the adopted D-139 subject requires each H item to have its own later D-000 cycle and commit, reinforced independently by D-138 for H2. Split the acts or explicitly review a scoped successor to that rule.
